source.title: A Learning Theoretic Perspective on Local Explainability
source.authors: Jeffrey Li; Vaishnavh Nagarajan; Gregory Plumb; A. Talwalkar

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies bounds on model performance and explanation generalization using local explanation fidelity. Its empirical results measure explanation fidelity, not the claim versions’ natural-label model train/test gap, interventions, or predictors of that gap.
record.gate_note: The empirical results concern train/test mirrored neighborhood fidelity (MNF) and neighborhood disjointedness for local explanations. The paper also cites prior work on deep-network generalization; those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study derives bounds using local explanation fidelity and measures explanation generalization on UCI regression datasets. Neither its theory nor its experiments test V1–V8. Neighborhood width is not network width, and MNF is explanation approximation error rather than classifier test error or magnitude-aware weight sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors derive separate bounds for model test MSE and held-out explanation MNF using local fidelity and neighborhood disjointedness. Experiments illustrate favorable disjointedness growth and explanation-gap trends, rather than directly validating model test-error predictions. The model-performance bound can become trivial in high dimensions and requires unlabeled test data.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies local explanation fidelity and its generalization, using neural networks as black-box models on UCI regression datasets; it does not use the model interventions or measures in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Neighborhood width affects the measured explanation generalization gap; the gap decreases with wider neighborhoods in most plots, while train MNF increases and test MNF decreases at certain width ranges.

fits_no_version.finding: Some explanation neighborhood widths permit approximately O(m^0.2) growth in neighborhood disjointedness without sharply increasing MNF or approaching a global linear explanation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local explanation neighborhoods can balance fidelity against the complexity arising from neighborhood disjointedness on the tested UCI regression datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Explanation train/test MNF gaps generally decrease with wider neighborhoods; training MNF increases while test MNF decreases over some width ranges.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider neighborhoods can improve held-out local explanation fidelity despite worsening training fidelity in finite-sample explanation learning.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (paper text says under review at ICLR 2021)
record.problems: The empirical results are described in aggregate across several UCI datasets, without dataset-specific numerical values in the supplied text; key results are plotted. The experiments concern explanation fidelity rather than the model generalization gaps in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were reported. Figure 1 and Figure 2 contain plotted results, but the text does not provide dataset-specific numerical values; the aggregate results described in Section 6 are recorded in R1–R3.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Network widening beyond zero training error and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Optimizer comparisons and their dependence on tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their penalty.
Dropout effects on classifier test error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations, their association with model generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and measuring retrained test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The rows' empirical findings are reported in the text, but their states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8. Citations to Zhang et al. and Neyshabur et al. supply background rather than new tests of their findings.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
Width sweeps of trained networks and test error past interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Batch-size effects on model test performance.
Dropout effects on classifier test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and the model train/test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring model test accuracy.

rows.subject: UCI regression datasets (aggregate; individual datasets are not identified in the supplied description)
rows.operation_detail: Varied neighborhood width and estimated the polynomial growth rate of the neighborhood disjointedness factor ρS across sample sizes.

conditions.value: several UCI regression datasets; individual datasets not stated
σ varied between the smallest and half the largest inter-example l2 distances

rows.measure: Estimated polynomial growth rate of ρS
rows.value: approximately O(m0.2) for some σ values, without g saturating or MNF metrics rising sharply
rows.note: Aggregate description of plotted results; no dataset-specific rates are stated. This measures a property of explanation neighborhoods, not model generalization gap.
rows.check: The reported approximate O(m^0.2) growth is correctly described, but neighborhood disjointedness does not measure any claim version. The experimental setup includes both unregularized and ExpO-trained black-box networks, which the recorded conditions omit.

rows.value: A generalization gap between train and test MNF exists.
